title: Rating Manipulation: Credibility Inversion and Audit Leakage
abstract: arXiv:2608.24062v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Online ratings turn a long review history into one public number. This makes sellers easier to compare, but it also gives them a single clear target to manipulate. We study a low-quality seller who can add fake reviews carrying different scores, buyers who infer quality from the displayed average, and a platform that can target particular scores for enforcement. The model separates the rating buyers see from the hidden mix of reviews used to produce it, and the two need not move together. An almost-perfect rating can be less credible than a slightly lower one when low-quality sellers are especially likely to manufacture the top of the scale, so a seller whose buyers become more valuable may display less and sell more. At a fixed displayed rating, targeted enforcement can redirect fake reviews toward other scores rather than eliminate manipulation; buyers do not see this substitution because the displayed average is unchanged. translated_title: 评分操纵：可信度反转与审计泄漏
translated_abstract: 在线评分将漫长的评论历史转化为一个公开的数字。这使得卖家更容易被比较，但也给了他们一个明确的目标去操纵。我们研究了一个低质量卖家，他能添加带有不同分数的虚假评论，买家从显示的平均值中推断质量，以及一个可以针对特定分数进行执法的平台。该模型将买家看到的评分与用于生成评分的隐藏评论混合体分离，这两者不必同步变化。当低质量卖家特别可能制造最高分时，近乎完美的评分可能比略低的评分更不可信，因此，当买家变得更有价值时，卖家可能显示更低的评分却卖出更多。在固定的显示评分下，针对性执法可以将虚假评论引向其他分数，而非消除操纵；买家看不到这种替代，因为显示的平均值未变。原始评分。
tldr: 本文揭示在线评分系统中，低质量卖家可通过操纵最高分使高评分反而降低可信度，且平台针对性执法可能只是转移虚假评论而非消除操纵。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that in online rating systems, low-quality sellers can manipulate top scores to make high ratings less credible, and targeted platform enforcement may merely redirect fake reviews rather than eliminate manipulation.
